title: Failed first snapshots leave persistent zero-version documents

evidence.quote: return undefined; // transient: editor mid-save or file temporarily gone

reasoning: Both local and Grist document creation persist the document row before proving that the initial snapshot can be captured. Local add ignores commitPath returning undefined on read/parse failure, then starts watching and returns success. Grist add writes the document and remote rows before awaiting syncRemote; if the network/auth call throws, the IPC reports failure but the half-added remote remains in the store. This creates documents with no usable first version and can break later flows that assume a head commit exists.
reproduction: Add an unsupported/corrupt file through docs:addPath, or connect Grist to a URL that fails after validation. The add operation either returns a tracked local document with versionCount 0 or throws while leaving a remote document row behind.
recommendation: Only persist a document after the initial snapshot succeeds, or wrap creation plus first commit/sync in a rollback-capable transaction. At minimum, if commitPath or syncRemote fails during add, delete the newly-created document row and surface the original error.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included smoke path adds only parseable local files and a successful mock Grist server; there is no failing initial snapshot or failing remote connect case.
suggestedRegressionTest: Assert that adding a corrupt local Office file and connecting to an unreachable Grist server both leave listDocuments unchanged and return a user-facing error.
minimumFixScope: DocumentService.addDocument and addGristDocument error handling around initial commit/sync.
